name: Fitzgerald's Genoa Junction
match_names: FITZGERALD'S GENOA JUNCTION OCTAGON HOUSE RESTAURANT
other_honors: Featured in Ron Faiola's book 'Wisconsin Supper Clubs: Another Round' (2016)
Listed on Ron Faiola's Wisconsin Supper Clubs List (wisconsinsupperclubs.com, 2026)
iconic_reason: Family-run restaurant in a Victorian octagon house on Genoa City's Main Street serving an all-you-can-eat Door County-style outdoor cod fish boil with BBQ chicken and ribs.
open_evidence: http://web.archive.org/web/20260124115932/https://fitzgeraldsfishboil.com/ - archived official site (Jan 24, 2026, (c) 2026) listed summer and winter hours; still on Ron Faiola's supper club list updated 2026-09-01; Overture Sept-2026 extract lists it as open. CAUTION: the live site returns a 'database connection' error (Sept 25, 2026) and an April 14, 2026 capture showed a 'Coming Soon / under construction' page, so current status is not directly confirmed.
notes: Open status is the least certain in this batch: no 2025-2026 news or dated post was reachable (web search budget exhausted; Yelp blocked). Founding year of the restaurant and the build year of the octagon house were not found; the site says it is one of the few remaining eight-sided Victorian houses. Business name on the site: Fitzgerald's Octagon House Inc.; TripAdvisor lists it as 'Fitzgerald's Genoa Junction Octagon House Restaurant'. Address given as 727 Main Street (Hwy B), 2 miles NW of Richmond, IL. A 2019 review mentioned a $15 flat all-you-can-eat price and cash only; no current price list found, so price_tier null. It is more a fish-boil restaurant than a classic supper club, but Faiola includes it.

name: The Ranch Supper Club
other_honors: Featured in Ron Faiola's book 'Wisconsin Supper Clubs: An Old-Fashioned Experience' (2013)
Featured in Ron Faiola's book 'Wisconsin Supper Clubs: Second Edition' (2023)
Listed on Ron Faiola's Wisconsin Supper Clubs List (wisconsinsupperclubs.com, 2026)
iconic_reason: Supper club east of Hayward that opened as The Aladdin in 1931 and has operated as The Ranch Supper Club since 1960.
open_evidence: No 2025-2026 dated evidence found: official site (c) 2018, last upload Nov 2022, says 'Open year-round Thursday - Sunday at 5pm'; newest dated diner review on Restaurantji is October 2024 (listing updated Sep 10, 2026 with hours, no closure noted). Still on Ron Faiola's 2026 list.
notes: 1931 is the business's own origin story (The Aladdin); renamed The Ranch Supper Club in 1960 under Vivian Levinson; Beth and Barney Morgan with Cheryl Haupt from 1987; now run by their daughter Haley and Nathan Bochler. Probably open but not confirmed with dated evidence, hence open=null. Located 1/4 mile east of Hayward on Hwy 77.

name: Mr. G's Supper Club
iconic_reason: Door County supper club on Highway 57 south of Jacksonport, run by the Geitner family since 1973 in the former Paldora Supper Club and Fernwood Gardens Ballroom.
open_evidence: Could not determine. The club's domain mrgslogancreekgrille.com no longer resolves (fetched 2026-09-25) and archived captures from Aug and Dec 2024 show the domain taken over by unrelated sites. Overture Sept-2026 still lists 'Mr. G's Supper Club' at 5890 State Highway 57 as open, but that field is often stale. Not on Ron Faiola's 2026 list.
notes: Came from the 'quick existence check' list; it's in Door County, not the Milwaukee area. Archived (2019) club site: 'Serving Door County Since 1973'; Bob and Lorraine Geitner bought it in 1973 when it was the Paldora Supper Club/Fernwood Gardens Ballroom; Bob Jr. and Mary bought it in 1981; open Fri-Sat evenings; also ran the Logan Creek Tiki Bar. 1973 is the Geitner/Mr. G's start; the Paldora Supper Club predates it (year unknown). The lapsed domain suggests it may have closed or changed hands; treat open status as unknown. Price tier unknown.

name: Anchor Bar and Grill
other_honors: Featured on Food Network's Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives (2011)
iconic_reason: Cash-only Tower Avenue tavern with a Lake Superior shipping theme, owned by the Anderson family since 1977 and known for two-thirds-pound burgers and fresh-cut fries.
open_evidence: https://www.superiortelegram.com/lifestyle/food-review-anchor-bar-and-grills-anchor-burger - Superior Telegram review May 10, 2023 (latest found); no 2025-2026 evidence found; Wikipedia describes it as operating
notes: 1977 is when Tom Anderson's family bought the building/bar (an older shipyard workers' bar); food service began in the 1980s. Owners Adam and Aaron Anderson. Wikipedia also cites inclusion in 'Hamburger America' and Gourmet magazine (June 2009) - not independently checked. Open status unconfirmed for 2025-2026. Overture also lists an 'Anchor Bar & Grill' at 103 E 7th St, Superior (likely a different/erroneous record).
